jobs.description:
About the Role

Wilverwater Digital Solutions is hiring a Front-End Developer in Santa Ana, CA, to create responsive, accessible and engaging web interfaces. You will work with designers, back-end developers and other technical team members to turn design concepts into functional web applications that deliver a consistent user experience.

This position involves developing interface components, integrating application features with back-end services, improving website performance and maintaining existing front-end applications. You will contribute to technical discussions, review implementation requirements and help ensure that new features work reliably across browsers and devices.

We are looking for a developer with practical experience in modern front-end technologies, sound coding practices and an eye for detail. The standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Key Responsibilities

* Develop and maintain responsive web interfaces using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript.
* Build interactive application features and reusable components using React, Angular or Vue.js.
* Convert UI/UX designs, wireframes and prototypes into functional front-end implementations.
* Connect front-end applications with REST APIs and back-end services.
* Ensure consistent website functionality across desktop, tablet and mobile devices.
* Write clean, reusable and maintainable code in accordance with project standards.
* Identify and resolve front-end defects, layout inconsistencies and browser compatibility issues.
* Improve page loading times, rendering performance and application responsiveness.
* Test new features and existing interfaces to verify functionality and visual accuracy.
* Work with designers to implement layouts, navigation elements and interactive components.
* Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback into development work.
* Use Git to manage code changes and collaborate through version control workflows.
* Maintain technical documentation and communicate development updates, issues and dependencies.

What We're Looking For

* Three or more years of professional experience in front-end or web application development.
* Strong knowledge of HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript.
* Hands-on experience with React, Angular or Vue.js.
* Understanding of responsive design, mobile-first development and cross-browser compatibility.
* Experience integrating REST APIs and handling JSON data.
* Familiarity with Git and collaborative development workflows.
* Knowledge of CSS frameworks or tools such as Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS or Sass.
* Understanding of web performance optimisation, debugging and front-end testing.
* Familiarity with web accessibility standards and usability principles.
* Ability to interpret design requirements and implement accurate user interfaces.
* Strong troubleshooting skills and attention to detail.
* Effective communication and the ability to work with designers, developers and project stakeholders.

What We Expect

We expect front-end implementations to meet agreed design specifications, function consistently across supported browsers and follow established coding standards. Changes should be tested before release, with attention to responsiveness, accessibility and performance.

When technical issues arise, we value clear communication, practical troubleshooting and a structured approach to resolving defects. Developers should be comfortable discussing implementation decisions, identifying potential limitations and contributing to improvements in the overall development process.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit their application through the job posting where they found this opportunity, following the employer's application instructions.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Wilverwater Digital Solutions considers applicants based on their job-related skills, experience and qualifications, in accordance with applicable employment laws.

* 401(k)

jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

**The Role:**

We're hiring one of the first software engineers on our electro-optical team. Today that means long-range EO/IR sensors. In future it could mean sensors on mobile and airborne platforms. Wherever the sensor sits, the job is the software that makes it, and every sensor around it, act as one system.

This is a software engineering role first. You don't need to be a camera or computer vision specialist. You do need to be an excellent engineer who is curious about physical systems and understands how real sensors behave: they drift, they disagree with each other, and a field test doesn't care what the simulation said.

You'll join a small, elite team that takes its own work into the field. You'll test live, change code live, and see how it holds up on the next flight. The capabilities you build will push the frontier of what these systems can do, and few engineers anywhere get to work this close to the hardware, the mission and the result.

We're also changing how we build software. The aim is to take a feature or a new capability and develop as much of it as possible without real hardware, then push it up the chain: through simulation, through hardware in the loop, and on to full end-to-end tests in the real world. Simulation will keep improving, but real hardware will always have the final say. So we're building the harnesses and graphs that carry a capability through every one of those stages, with AI doing as much of the work as it can be trusted with. The end state is fully autonomous, end-to-end tests run against real hardware at our test sites. This is what you'll be building.

**What You'll Build:**

* Software that works on any sensor. Code that stays generic across many different camera heads and configurations while still hitting its performance bar, and flexes to whatever the mission and the customer demand.
* The path from desk to field. Harnesses and graphs that take a capability from first commit through simulation and hardware in the loop to a full end-to-end test, with as little manual effort as possible.
* Autonomous field testing. The system that runs complete tests against real hardware at our test sites on its own, and reports back what happened.
* Better simulation and replay. So more of every feature can be built and proven before it touches hardware.
* Multi-sensor integration. The interfaces, timing and data flow that let radar, cameras and other sensors work as one system.
* Fielded software. Deployment, monitoring and live fixes for systems running on edge hardware at test and customer sites.

  

**This Role Is Not:**

* Algorithm research. You'll build and ship software, not invent new detection or tracking algorithms.
* Physics modeling. You won't be building high-fidelity physics models in MATLAB or Simulink.
* Applied machine learning. You won't be training models on sensor data.
* Pure DevOps. You'll run infrastructure, but most of your time goes into writing software other engineers depend on.

  

**What We're Looking For:**

We care more about strong engineering fundamentals and curiosity than about any specific technology or domain.

* 3+ years of professional software engineering, including owning a production system end to end: you designed it, shipped it, and fixed it when it broke.
* A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Strong Python. You build services and tools other engineers depend on, not just scripts and notebooks.
* Comfort with Linux, Docker, networking and CI. You can get a multi-service system running on hardware you've never touched before.
* Real leverage from AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, with a considered view on what to delegate to them and what not to. We treat them as a multiplier on skills you already have: you should be able to write, explain and debug your own code without them.
* Grounding in the physical world, whether from an engineering degree, hands-on work with hardware, sensors or robotics, or field time with systems that had to work outside the lab. You can read a schematic, understand a test rack, and talk to an optics or RF engineer.
* An appetite for field work. You want to be on site when your code runs, and you can debug and ship a fix before the next flight.
* A habit of measuring rather than guessing: you build the experiment, then trust the data.

**Nice to Have:**

* Cameras, EO/IR sensors, gimbals, radar, or video pipelines such as GStreamer or DeepStream.
* Embedded Linux or edge computing, especially NVIDIA Jetson, and GPU or CUDA work.
* Robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones or aerospace.

* Building AI agent harnesses or workflow graphs.

jobs.description:
### **Description**

Impulse Space is seeking a **Embedded Linux Software Engineer** to develop and maintain the foundational software stack that powers our avionics platforms. This role requires deep expertise in embedded Linux, low-level hardware/software integration, and platform engineering practices to ensure secure, reliable, and maintainable systems.

### **Responsibilities**

  

* **Linux Distribution Development:**
  + Build, configure, and maintain a Yocto-based Linux distribution for custom avionics hardware.
  + Manage kernel configuration, system services, and integration of middleware components.
* **Board Bring-Up & Hardware Integration:**
  + Perform initial board bring-up of avionics computers.
  + Debug hardware/software integration issues across CPU, memory, and peripheral subsystems.
* **Driver Development & Debugging:**
  + Develop, port, and maintain Linux device drivers for sensors, communication buses, and memory devices.
  + Debug kernel-space and user-space interactions using hardware debuggers and tracing tools.
* **Platform Engineering & System Hardening:**
  + Implement secure boot and code signing for flight-critical binaries.
  + Configure and manage router certificates and other cryptographic assets.
  + Apply Linux security frameworks such as AppArmor and SELinux for mandatory access control.
  + Design and maintain OTA update infrastructure with rollback/A-B partitioning support.
  + Manage system configuration, startup scripts, and fault-tolerant resource allocation.

  

### **Minimum Qualifications**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degrees.
* Experience building and maintaining Yocto-based embedded Linux distributions for custom boards.
* Demonstrated ability to develop, configure, and debug Linux kernel drivers.
* Demonstrated experience developing in C/C++, with ability to work in constrained, low-level environments.

### **Preferred Skills and Experience**

  

* Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation, design reviews, and cross-discipline collaboration.
* Experience with UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, and similar buses.
* Strong understanding of embedded software principles, real-time constraints, and resource-limited systems.
* Experience with OTA update design and deployment (e.g., dual-partition or rollback-safe systems).
* Familiarity with system hardening and security frameworks (SELinux, AppArmor, secure boot, TPM/cryptographic key management).
* Experience with CI/CD pipelines for embedded systems (e.g., GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI).
* Familiarity with containerization and reproducible build techniques for embedded platforms.
* Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, hardware debuggers, and signal analyzers.

**Additional Information:**  
  
Compensation bands are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual level and base pay is determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities and internal equity. In addition to base salary, for full-time hires, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the **form of stock options**, and access to **medical, vision & dental coverage** as well as **access to a 401(k) retirement plan**.
  
  
Impulse Space’s spacecraft manufacturing business is subject to U.S. export regulations including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR). This position requires applicants to be either U.S. Persons (i.e., U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent U.S. resident (green card holder), an individual granted asylum in the U.S., or an individual admitted in U.S. refugee status) or persons eligible to obtain an export license from the U.S. Departments of State, Commerce, or other applicable U.S. government agencies. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Impulse Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Impulse Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

### **About Impulse Space**

Impulse Space, the in-space transportation company founded by Tom Mueller, is opening access beyond Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with its fleet of in-space transportation vehicles. The high-energy Helios vehicle unlocks orbits beyond LEO with its powerful Deneb engine, dropping off payloads in MEO, GEO, heliocentric, lunar, and other planetary orbits. The flight-proven Mira vehicle uses a nontoxic, high-impulse chemical propulsion system to offer orbital transport, constellation deployment, and precision reentry services to customers throughout LEO. Led by a team that delivered the most reliable rockets in history, Impulse provides economical and efficient in-space transportation by reliably and rapidly getting customers where they want to go.

**Job Title:** Sr. Software Engineer, Agents

**Team:** Engineering

**Location:** Onsite - Sawtelle (Between Santa Monica & West LA)

**Employment Type:** Full-time, Salary, Exempt

**Reports To:** Head of Engineering

### **About Plug**

Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We’ve raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

### **Why Plug**

* You’ll help build the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
* You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
* You’ll be part of an AI-native company. We’re rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.
* You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
* You’ll ship constantly, with high autonomy and a direct line to company outcomes.

### **The Opportunity**

Plug runs on a lot of manual work: reading titles and inspection reports, chasing paperwork with dealers, checking vehicle details, answering sellers, and moving each car from offer to sale. Much of that work can be done by agents. We already run LLM features in production, and our engineers own the core platform: the marketplace, pricing, and the systems that tie them together. What we need now is someone who can turn a stream of real operational problems into agents that work reliably, one after another.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Build and ship agents and multi-agent workflows for operations, dealers, and sellers: document extraction, inspection and title review, dealer and seller communication, and internal tooling.
* Use LangChain and LangGraph to build agents, and LangSmith or Langfuse to trace, debug, and evaluate them.
* Write evals, build datasets from real cases, measure accuracy and failure modes, and make regressions visible.
* Integrate agents with the services the team already owns, through clean APIs and tools. Work within the existing architecture and raise design concerns with the owning engineer instead of routing around them.
* Monitor agents in production: cost, latency, error rates, and human-review rates. Fix what breaks and tighten prompts, tools, and guardrails over time.
* Ship full-stack when the job calls for it: the TypeScript and React screens where people review and correct agent output, and the backend endpoints behind them.
* Help the rest of engineering adopt the same patterns. Build reusable tools, examples, and short write-ups that make the next agent faster to build.

### **What You’ll Bring**

* 5+ years of full-time industry software engineering, with a track record of shipping features to production and supporting them after launch.
* Strong TypeScript or Python, and comfort working across the stack: APIs, databases, and frontend when needed.
* Hands-on experience building LLM features in production: tool use, retrieval, structured output, and above all, evaluation.
* Experience with an agent framework and observability stack, ideally LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, or Langfuse. If you’ve used something else, show us what you built and how you knew it worked.
* You work agent-first. You’ve built your own tooling around coding agents, such as skills, MCP servers, custom workflows, or evals.
* Comfort building inside systems other people designed. You can disagree, make your case, and then ship the agreed plan.
* A habit of writing things down: short design notes, eval results, and runbooks that others can pick up.
* You enjoy being part of a small team: pairing, reviewing each other’s work, and sharing credit.
* High agency in an ambiguous, fast-moving startup. You find the most valuable workflow to automate and ship against it without waiting for a perfect spec.
* BS in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

### **Nice to Have**

* Experience with document-heavy workflows such as titles, registrations, inspections, lending, or insurance.
* Experience with vehicle, marketplace, or auction products.
* Experience with human-in-the-loop review tools, or with fine-tuning and prompt optimization for production LLM features.

### **Compensation and Benefits**

Annual salary: $175,000 to $200,000

Salary ranges come from independent, third-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs, and market conditions. We review ranges periodically and may adjust them as the market changes.

### **Benefits & Perks**

* Health, Vision, and Dental insurance
* 401(k) plan
* Daily lunch stipend
* Equity (based on role and performance)
* 30-day remote work from anywhere policy
* Unlimited PTO
* Fully stocked kitchen
* Dog-friendly office
* Ongoing opportunities for growth and development

This full-time position is an in-person role based in Sawtelle (between Santa Monica and West Los Angeles). Relocation assistance will not be provided for successful candidates. Sponsorship not available at this time.

We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, marital status, military or veteran status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. **About Northwood:**

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

**Role**

Northwood engineers and operators run hardware and software across a global network of antenna ground stations and the cloud services behind them. No one sells a platform for running a network like this at scale, so Northwood builds its own.

Platform Engineering builds the software that takes Northwood products from first prototype to full operation. That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. Every one of these problems has to work across every site, service, and customer at once.

Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow.

As an early-career Software Engineer on the Platform team, you'll ship to real production systems from your first weeks, with close mentorship, and take on more ownership as you show you're ready. You don't need to know every part of the stack today. You need to learn fast, reason clearly through problems you haven't seen before, and care a lot about what you build.

**Key areas of focus**

You'll work across these areas over time. No one is expected to own everything listed.

* **Delivery and release**

  + Build the CI and release pipelines that take code from commit to production, in the cloud and at ground stations around the world.
  + Make shipping safe and continuous, with staged rollouts and fast rollback, so no one has to test in production.
* **Simulation and test**

  + Build simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, so every release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site.
  + Build tools that replay real recorded data through the system to catch problems early.
* **Ground station operations**

  + Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, and updated, in remote locations with few or no people on site.
  + Write software that runs on the servers that sit next to the antennas, and keep a global fleet of them healthy.
* **Observability**

  + Build the monitoring, logging, and alerting that show the health of every service and site.
  + Turn raw telemetry into signals engineers and operators can act on before a problem reaches a customer.
* **Internal platform and tools**

  + Build the backend services and web interfaces engineers and operators use every day to create, ship, and run software.
  + Talk directly with the people who use what you build, and turn their feedback into improvements.
* **Infrastructure and security**

  + Define the cloud and site infrastructure the platform runs on as code.
  + Build identity, secrets management, and least-privilege access into the platform, so every service gets them by default.

**Basic Qualifications**

* 0 to 2 years of professional software experience. It doesn't have to be a full-time role. Internships, research, open source, and projects outside the classroom all count, so tell us about them.
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, math, or a related field. This is a soft requirement: if you didn't pursue a degree, tell us what you did instead.
* Has written real software in at least one general-purpose language (such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or C++) beyond required coursework.
* Has built and shipped something other people used or relied on.
* Has solved a hard technical problem largely on their own, such as debugging a non-obvious failure or designing a system from scratch.

* **Languages:** proficiency in one or more languages (such as Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript), with opinions about which one fits which job.
